    {
      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 6, Section fact_sheet",
      "exact_span": "EPA was unable to approve section 20.6.4.98 of the NMWQS because the State did not submit a Use Attainable Assessment (UAA) to support an aquatic life designation that does not meet the CWA §101(a)(2) objective as required by 40 CFR 131.10(j)(1).",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Whether interim segment standards are federally approvable or superseded affects which criteria may be enforced as numeric limits and how missing or non-numeric evidence for aquatic-life-related parameters should be classified when compliance cannot be directly compared."
    },
    {
      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 6, Section fact_sheet",
      "exact_span": "Prior to submittal of UAA, the designated uses of the downstream perennial stream are applicable to the receiving water. Therefore, chronic aquatic life criteria are appropriate for RP screening.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,B,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "This interim rule substitutes downstream perennial-stream uses and chronic aquatic life criteria for RP screening; different readings of when the UAA trigger applies, what 'downstream perennial stream' means, or what 'RP screening' requires could change which WQBEL are imposed (A), whether additional reasonable-potential monitoring or studies are obligated (B), and how to treat periods without numeric results tied to aquatic-life criteria (C)."
    },
    {
      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 6, Section fact_sheet",
      "exact_span": "Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44(d) require limits in addition to, or more stringent than effluent limitation guidelines (technology based). State WQS that are more stringent than effluent limitation guidelines are as follows:",
      "affected_purpose": "A",
      "computation_change_reason": "This is the operative gate for imposing water quality-based limits beyond technology-based effluent guidelines; whether a parameter's state WQS is 'more stringent' determines if an enforceable numeric limit must be included and compared to measurements."
    },
    {
      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 6, Section fact_sheet",
      "exact_span": "The previous permit established limits for total aluminum and total copper. These limits will be maintained.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Directly states that total aluminum and total copper numeric limits carry forward; interpretation of 'maintained' (same values, same parameters, same enforceability) determines which measurement/limit pairs are evaluated and how absent Al/Cu results are categorized relative to known obligations."
    },
    {
      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",
      "locator": "Page 6, Section fact_sheet",
      "exact_span": "In accordance with 40 CFR 122.45(c), total recoverable metal concentration must be established as effluent limitations.",
      "affected_purpose": "A,C",
      "computation_change_reason": "Specifies the measurement basis (total recoverable) for metal effluent limitations; comparing reported dissolved, total, or other speciation results to limits would change exceedance determinations and whether available evidence is adequate for compliance comparison."
    },

      "source": "gcc/fact_sheet.pdf",

      "exact_span": "The exceptions listed in that sub-section refers to technology-",

    }
  ]
}
